exposure: Mode of delivery (normal vaginal delivery vs. other)
outcome: Breastfeeding continuation (duration, specifically 6 months or longer)
cohort: The study included 48 women with epilepsy treated in the epilepsy clinic at King Abdullah Medical City from 2019 to June 2023.
finding: The rate of breastfeeding among women with epilepsy in the Makkah region is low, with significant factors including the number of ASMs, seizure control during pregnancy, mode of delivery, and urban residency.
mod_finding: Normal vaginal delivery was significantly associated with a higher rate of breastfeeding (81.3%) compared to other modes of birth (43.8%).
cross-section timing: Data was collected from 2019 to June 2023
